Visiting Academic Policy                                                                                       Version 1.0 | P a g e  4  
 
1 Introduction/Context 
It can be mutually advantageous for South East Technological University (SETU) and persons 
who have achieved excellence in their respective fields to enter into a formal collaborative 
agreement. Such persons of distinction will contribute their unique expertise to the 
University.  They may also assist the University in advancing its strategic goals. Appointees 
will include individuals distinguished by high achievement in the world of industry, business, 
science, the professions, the arts, or public service who have been recognised by peers as 
outstanding in their field. 
2 Purpose  
This policy aims to enhance academic collaborations and attract those who can make a 
valuable contribution to engage with the University in areas such as scholarship, research, 
development or other valuable contributing activities.   
3 Scope  
This policy applies to the awarding of Visiting positions to the University. It outlines the 
process for such appointments and the responsibilities and expectations of appointees. 
Appointments are strategic and for a defined period. They are specific to a particular 
faculty/department/research institute/centre. As visiting positions are not considered as 
staff, they are not remunerated and are not awarded on the basis of a competition.  
4 Principles  
Holders of academic posts in other institutions will assume a Visiting title equivalent to that 
which they hold in their home institution (i.e., their primary employer). They may be given 
the Visiting title of Visiting Professor/ Visiting Lecturer/ Visiting Research Fellow as relevant.  
Those not employed in an academic institution (fields of commerce, business, industry, law, 
public administration, politics, etc.) may be appointed to Visiting Fellow in which case they 
should have post-graduate qualifications and/or high-level of professional expertise. 
When completing the nomination form, the nominator can choose the appropriate title 
based on academic/professional rank and level of academic/industry experience of the 
applicant. Please refer to Appendix C for definitions and criteria to ensure the correct title is 
proposed.  
4.1 
Terms of Appointment  
• Appointees will be appointed for a maximum period of five years.  
• Appointments may be ended by mutual consent or by either party.  
• Appointments in Faculty/Institute/Centres may be renewed following a review by 
the Executive Management Team (EMT). 
• Any amendments to the terms and conditions of the visiting appointment during the 
agreed period should be reviewed by HR and the relevant Head of Faculty/Executive 
Sponsor.

Visiting Academic Policy                                                                                       Version 1.0 | P a g e  5  
 
• In exceptional circumstances the University reserves the right to withdraw the 
appointment; (see section 4.2 of this policy).   
Appointees will be expected to maintain the highest ethical standards when representing the 
University; Individuals who are awarded an appointment will:  
• Not have any entitlements to remuneration or pension benefits; 
• Be entitled to an appropriate office or laboratory space; 
• Not be eligible to be a member of the Academic Council; 
• 
Be expected to make themselves familiar with and be bound by the University’s 
policies and procedures available here https://www.setu.ie/policies. 
 
SETU (South East Technological University) is an equal opportunity employer. SETU is 
committed to promoting equality, diversity, and inclusion in all aspects of its operations, 
including recruitment and employment. 
 
Appointees may be eligible for travel and/or subsistence expenses related to work 
undertaken on behalf of the University (only with the prior approval of the relevant Vice 
President or Head of Faculty). Breaches of any University policies may result in the withdrawal 
of the appointment. 
 
4.2 
Termination of Appointment 
The appointment may be terminated if: 
• 
Either party issues a month’s notice in writing to the other party; 
• 
An appointee engages in conduct which is likely to bring the reputation of the 
University into disrepute. 
5 Policy Details  
5.1 
Roles and Responsibilities of Appointees  
Appointees may be invited by the Faculty/Institute/Centre to carry out the following 
functions. 
• Collaborate and assist in the professional training of students through fieldwork, 
projects or guest lecturing;  
• Collaborate in research, invited and/or sponsored by existing faculty with whom they 
have close working relationships;  
• Contribute to the scholarly understanding of a subject area in a field otherwise not 
available within the University;   
• Attend the University at such times as are necessary to meet any commitments 
associated with the appointment;  
• Operate within the framework of the University’s policies and procedures in their 
role as a Visiting appointee.

Visiting Academic Policy                                                                                       Version 1.0 | P a g e  6  
 
An appointee must:  
• Ensure that there is no conflict of interest between their appointment at the University 
and any outside work or activities and their engagement with the University (if 
applicable);  
• Comply with the University’s policies including export controls, intellectual property 
requirements and any requirements regarding data, research ethics, research 
integrity, and publication. 
• Acknowledge appointment status in academic attributions related to the 
appointment; and  
• Attribute their academic publications to the University in accordance with the 
requirements of the University’s Authorship and Data Retention Policy and 
Procedures.  
An appointee may not:  
• Authorise the expenditure of university funds; and/or  
• Commit the University to any contractual or other legally binding agreement. 
 
5.1 
Privileges of a Visiting Appointee 
The following will apply to Individuals who are awarded an appointment:  
• Where practicable, access to the University’s library, IT resources and email facilities 
will be provided as part of the Appointee set up processes.  
• For communication purposes, appointees will be kept up-to-date and appropriately 
informed by their relevant Department, Faculty or Research Institute/Group/Centre. 
• When used in any documentation (including digital platforms/ opinion posts), the 
relevant appointment title must be used in its entirety, so the appointment is of a 
Visiting nature, e.g., on business cards, correspondence and publications. To avoid 
misrepresentation, the appointee must not abbreviate the title conferred by the 
University.  
• Appointees may use their association with the University for the purpose of external 
applications for funding, but such funds must be administered by the University and 
the use of such funds must be governed by the same regulations as apply to other 
research income. 
 
6 Responsibility and Authority   
 
6.1 
Appointment procedure 
Nominations for Visiting appointments must be made to a Head of Faculty/Executive Sponsor 
who will then bring them for consideration to the VP People Culture & EDI.  
Nominations are made by submitting a copy of the nominee’s CV and a completed Visiting 
Academic Nomination Form (see sample in Appendix A) to the  chosen Head of Faculty/ 
Executive Sponsor and should indicate:

Visiting Academic Policy                                                                                       Version 1.0 | P a g e  7  
 
• The way in which the nominee will contribute to the enhancement of the University’s 
teaching, research and/or professional activities;  
• The qualities, standing and achievements the nominee possesses that are deemed 
appropriate for consideration, and those which are considered comparable to those 
expected at the relevant University level;  
• The category, level and term of appointment proposed;  
• Confirmation that arrangements made regarding Intellectual Property (if appropriate) 
comply with the SETU Policy on Intellectual Property;  
• Any additional facilities or resources that are to be provided by the Faculty/Research 
Centre or Institute over and above normal requirements. 
 
If the Head of Faculty/Executive Sponsor is satisfied that the appointment will benefit the 
Faculty/Institute and University, they will: 
• Recommend the nomination and title of appointment for approval. 
The Executive Sponsor will then forward a memo accompanying a copy of the appointee’s CV 
along with a completed and signed Visiting Academic Nomination Form via email to 
VPPeoplecultureedi@setu.ie  for consideration at the next available sitting of Recruitment 
Committee for approval. 
 
The appointee and relevant Head of Faculty/Executive Sponsor will be notified by letter of 
the decision by the HR department. 
If successful; 
HR will issue a letter of appointment, outlining the period, terms and privileges attached to 
the appointment including the appointee’s ID Number. HR will issue  SETU Card, library access, 
email account, and look after CORE set-up etc. 
 
Following appointment, the relevant Head of Faculty/Executive Sponsor will ensure that 
arrangements are in place in relation to university induction, building relationships and 
understanding and fulfilling expectations for the appointee. 
HR will record the period approved and the appointment will expire on that date unless 
notified earlier by the individual or the Executive Sponsor that the appointment has been 
terminated sooner or in the event that a renewal request is lodged by the Executive Sponsor/ 
Head of Faculty. It is the responsibility of the Executive Sponsor/ Head of Faculty to lodge a 
request for renewal of the appointment in line with the application process in advance of the 
date of expiry of the original appointment. 
The relevant Head of Faculty/Executive sponsor must request all extensions to be noted by 
the Recruitment Committee.

Visiting Academic Policy                                                                                       Version 1.0 | P a g e  8  
 
6.2 
Confidentiality 
The University is obliged to maintain confidentiality in its work. It is the duty of the 
appointee to observe such confidentiality.  This restriction shall continue to apply after 
termination of this appointment in line with SETU’s GDPR Policy. 
7 Compliance 
It is expected that all employees of the University and all members of the University 
Governing Body will comply with this policy. 
8 Useful Links 
Policies page 
9 Review of Policy  
This policy will be reviewed in advance of the review date, and/or as soon as possible 
following new or updated legislation, national or sectoral policy. 
10 Policy Author 
Any feedback or issues arising on the implementation of this policy should be communicated 
to the policy authors, Office of VP People Culture & EDI. 
The Office of VP People Culture & EDI are responsible for ensuring that the Policy Owner (HR) 
is aware of these comments when reviewing the policy.

11.3 Appendix C: Definitions and Criteria  
 
Visiting academics are not appointed on the basis of a competition and, as Visiting academics/fellows 
SETU is not their primary employer. Visiting academics/fellows have a non-permanent affiliation with the 
University.  
Visiting appointees as well as being leading academics in their field can include the following categories: 
Individuals distinguished by high achievement in the world of industry, business, science, the professions, 
the arts or public service who have been recognised by peers as outstanding in their field.  
Visiting Professors, with sufficient academic experience may act as co-supervisors of research students, 
subject to the approval of the Head of Graduate Studies.  
Criteria for appointment:   
Holders of academic posts in other institutions will assume a Visiting title equivalent to that which they 
hold in their home institution (i.e. their primary employer). They may be given the Visiting title of Visiting 
Professor/ Visiting Lecturer / Visiting Research Fellow as relevant (see Table 1).  
Those not employed in an academic institution (fields of commerce, business, industry, law, public 
administration, politics, etc.) may be appointed to a Visiting Fellow in which case they should have post-
graduate qualifications and/or high-level of professional expertise. 
Table 1: Criteria for Appointment by Title   
 
Level  
Criteria  
Visiting Professor  The appointee must hold an appointment at a professorial level in a recognised university 
or comparable institution of higher education; or be distinguished by high achievement in 
an area of expertise related to the proposing department’s discipline area(s). 
Visiting Lecturer 
The appointee will be working, or have worked, at an equivalent level (lecturer/senior 
lecturer) in a recognised university or comparable institution of higher education; or be 
distinguished by high achievement in an area of expertise related to the proposing 
department’s discipline area(s).  
Visiting Research 
Fellow  
 
 
 
The appointee must hold a PhD and have a body of peer-reviewed published research or 
have equivalent senior research experience or hold an appointment to a position in a 
partner organisation (e.g. HSE/Teagasc) where research is a formal requirement of their 
role. The nature of the research must be relevant to the work of the proposing 
department.   
Visiting Fellow  
This title is for those not employed in an academic institution (fields of commerce, 
business, industry, law, public administration, politics, etc.) may be appointed to a Visiting 
Fellow in which case they should have post-graduate qualifications and/or high-level of 
professional expertise. 
  
Details of the criteria set out above need to be explicit in the nomination form.
